questions.q: What are the four stages text moves through in a transformer-based LLM?
options: Tokenize, embed, attend, predict
Compile, link, execute, output
Encrypt, transmit, decrypt, display
Parse, index, search, rank
questions.explain: Every transformer-based LLM tokenizes the input, embeds tokens as vectors, runs self-attention, then predicts the next token's probability distribution.

questions.q: What does self-attention compute for each token?
options: A weighted relevance score against every other token in the sequence
A spell-check correction for that token
The token's exact dictionary definition
A random number used only for training
questions.explain: Self-attention produces, for every token, a learned weight describing how relevant each other token is to it — regardless of distance.

questions.q: Why did transformers replace RNNs for most language modeling?
options: RNNs process text sequentially and lose long-range context; transformers process a whole sequence in parallel
RNNs require more memory per word than transformers
Transformers don't require any training data
RNNs cannot run on GPUs at all
questions.explain: RNNs carry one running summary forward word by word, which is slow and degrades over long distances. Transformers connect any two tokens directly and process the sequence in parallel.

questions.q: In the sentence "The cat sat because it was tired," what should self-attention do for the word "it"?
options: Give "it" a low weight toward every other word equally
Weight "it" strongly toward "cat", since that's the pronoun's likely referent
Delete "it" from the sequence entirely
Only compare "it" to the very next word
questions.explain: Self-attention should connect "it" strongly to "cat" so the model resolves what the pronoun refers to, even though the words are several positions apart.

questions.q: Why are GPUs well-suited to running transformer models?
options: GPUs are built for massively parallel computation, matching how transformers process a whole sequence at once
GPUs are the only hardware that can store text data
GPUs process tokens one at a time, like an RNN
GPUs were specifically invented for language models in 2017
questions.explain: Transformers process every token's attention calculations in parallel, which maps naturally onto a GPU's architecture of many simultaneous small computations.
